guarantees.claim: iv_d is assigned iv when iv_sel equals IV_INPUT.
iv_d is assigned data_out_d when iv_sel equals IV_DATA_OUT.
iv_d is assigned aes_transpose(state_out) when iv_sel equals IV_DATA_OUT_RAW.
iv_d is assigned data_in_prev_q when iv_sel equals IV_DATA_IN_PREV.
iv_d is assigned ctr when iv_sel equals IV_CTR.
iv_d is assigned prd_clearing_data when iv_sel equals IV_CLEAR.
iv_d is assigned prd_clearing_data for any iv_sel value not covered by explicit cases.
guarantees.cond: default (iv_sel not matching any explicit case)

uncertain_points.claim: Fallback assignment to prd_clearing_data for iv_d when iv_sel is invalid (or explicitly IV_CLEAR) may propagate pseudo-random clearing data into the IV path, potentially weakening security if prd_clearing_data is predictable or not a cryptographically strong random value.
uncertain_points.cond: iv_sel != any defined enum value or iv_sel == IV_CLEAR
uncertain_points.risk: Predictable or non-cryptographic IV could compromise AES operation, enabling ciphertext correlation attacks or secret disclosure.

uncertain_points.claim: If iv_sel receives an illegal value due to a fault, the block silently outputs prd_clearing_data with no error signal or alert, possibly masking the fault while still outputting data that could be exploited.
uncertain_points.cond: iv_sel is invalid and no error reporting is present
uncertain_points.risk: Fault goes undetected; an attacker could trigger illegal IV selection to force predictable IV output or cause unexpected cipher state.

uncertain_points.claim: The default branch may be unreachable if the iv_sel enumeration contains exactly the six defined values and no other encoding. Need to check enum definition to determine if default is dead code or intended for X/Z/other values.
uncertain_points.risk: Dead code could be optimized away or reflect a misunderstanding; if reachable, the prd_clearing_data fallback was intended for robustness.
